verdict.rationale: ROS 2 has built-in DDS-Security support through sros2. Security enclaves each encapsulate a policy for protecting ROS communications, and participants are authenticated and their traffic encrypted using a keystore. That is first-party, communication-level access control, which can restrict which participants interact with a robot's graph. It is not an operator-facing roles-and-permissions system for people commanding, configuring, or viewing individual robots. missing for 10: human user/role-based access management, documented per-topic/service/parameter permission mapping to command/configure/view actions, per-robot permission administration, independent or hands-on corroboration.
